page: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor architecture, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth for small-block cached reads is also in the top tier, while large-block reads and writes register as strong. In cryptographic and integer operations, the CPU utilizes advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES. For language model workloads, the instance delivers top-tier prompt processing speeds for small models and strong text generation speeds for medium and large models.

From a resource density perspective, the m7a.16xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy general-purpose workloads due to its dedicated physical cores and high-speed DDR5 memory. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-intensive applications. This instance is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
